note: A grader sees results.tex and the step 7.6 rule text only. This file is the key and must never be shown to a grader.

S01.label: negative
S01.why: Method section, out of scope; also not a performance claim.

S02.label: negative
S02.why: Setup detail, not a performance claim.

S03.label: negative
S03.why: Carries \cite -- 7.5's lane (claim<->citation), explicitly out of 7.6's scope.

S04.label: negative
S04.why: Reports what a table contains; makes no claim about our method.

S05.label: negative
S05.why: HARD. Anchor (\ref{tab:main}) is in the paragraph, not the sentence. 7.6 says sentence OR paragraph.

S06.label: positive
S06.why: 'substantially more robust' with no \ref and no numeral anywhere near.

S07.label: positive
S07.why: 'demonstrates ... universally superior' off a single table.

S08.label: negative
S08.why: HARD. 'suggests' over a 1.4-point anchor is a calibrated verb -- §2.5 says this is the correct outcome, not a defect.

S09.label: negative
S09.why: HARD. Numeral anchor with no \ref. 7.6 accepts a reported number as an anchor.

S10.label: positive
S10.why: 'improves considerably' -- vague magnitude, no number, no ref. Same claim as S09 stripped of its anchor.

S11.label: positive
S11.why: 'proves ... necessary' off one ablation, despite real numbers.

S12.label: positive
S12.why: 'establishes the general effectiveness' from one table row.

S13.label: positive
S13.why: 'confirms ... any distribution shift' off one figure.

S15.label: negative
S15.why: HARD. 'demonstrates' is legitimate here -- the anchor spans three tables, so the verb does not exceed it.

S17.label: negative
S17.why: HARD. Limitation, correctly hedged ('may not transfer'). §2.5 protects hedging.
